sentences.text: The present DAR was filed on 31.08.2024 which was treated as a claim petition.
The Road Traffic Accident in question took place on 02.06.2024 at about 06:00 PM at Vikas Marg, Laxmi Nagar to ITO, near IP Estate Police Station, Delhi.

Mr. Ganpat Lal (hereinafter referred to as the petitioner) had suffered grievous injuries in the said accident which was allegedly caused by vehicle bearing registration No.
TS-15EZ-6666 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle).

The said vehicle was being driven by respondent no. 1 Mr. Poleboina Rahul;
owned by respondent No.2 Mr. Poleboina Krishna and insured with respondent no.3, United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
BRIEF FACTS 2.

The brief facts that have emerged from the DAR are that on 02.06.2024, on receipt of information of an accident vide GD No.83A the information of present accident was received by the IO/ASI Anil Kumar.

Thereafter, he along with HC Manish went to the LNJP Hospital, where they collected the two MLCs, one MLC pertaining to injured Ganpat Lal bearing no.116321455/24 and another MLC pertaining to injured Santosh bearing no.116321456.
Injured Ganpat Lal had told to the IO that he will give his statement after consulting with his family members.

The other injured namely Santosh,
who is wife of injured Ganpat Lal also said the same.
Therefore, the call was kept pending.

Thereafter on 06.06.2024 vide Diary no.3398, IO received a complaint regarding the present accident from complainant Santosh Devi disclosing the details of the offending vehicle.
On the complaint of Santosh Devi, IO registered the FIR against the driver of the offending vehicle u/s.279/337 IPC.
During the course of investigation, IO prepared the site plan at the instance of complainant Santosh Devi.
IO had taken the accidental motorcycle into his custody.
No CCTV Camera was found at the spot of accident.
Thereafter, IO served the notice under Section 133 MV Act to the owner of the offending vehicle.
IO also served the notice u/s. 41A CrPC upon the driver of the offending vehicle.
4. On 04.07.2024, injured Ganpat Lal came to the police station for release of his motorcycle on superdari as well as to enquire about the progress of the present matter.
There, he found the driver of the offending vehicle sitting in the PS.
Injured Ganpat Lal identified the driver of the offending vehicle.
Thereafter, IO interrogated the driver of the offending vehicle.
After interrogation, IO bound down the driver of the offending vehicle for further investigation.
Thereafter, the offending vehicle was taken into the custody of the IO and deposited the same into the maalkhana.
Mechanical inspection of both the vehicles i.e. offending vehicle as well as the motorcycle of the injured were got conducted.
The documents pertaining to both the vehicles were got verified from the concerned authorities.
The same were found to be correct.
Thereafter, both the MLCs of injured persons were submitted for the final opinion.
The doctor had opined the injury as "Grievous" in the MLC of injured Ganpat Lal and "Simple" in the MLC of Santosh Devi.
Thereafter, IO added the Section 338 IPC in the present matter.

sentences.text: The onus to prove this issue was on the petitioner.

It is the case of the petitioner that on 02.06.2024 at about 06.00 P.M., when the petitioner alongwith his wife were going on their motorcycleto Palam, they reached Vikas Marg, Laxmi Nagar to ITO, Near IP Estate Police Station,
Delhi.
Suddenly, the offending vehicle being driven rashly and negligently by respondent no. 1 hit their motorcycle from behind due to which the petitioner fell on the road and received injuries.
He has stated that he was taken to the LNJP, Delhi for treatment.
The petitioner has reiterated these facts on oath as PW-1 by way of his affidavit Ex. PW1/A.
It is submitted by Ld. Counsel for the petitioner that in view of the facts and circumstances, the accident and the rash and negligent act of respondent no. l has been proved.
16. Record perused.
17. In the present matter, the petitioner as PW1 specifically stated that his motorcycle was hit by the offending vehicle.
He remained firm on his testimony and his testimony could not be shaken by the detailed cross-examination done by the respondent no. 3.
The respondents no. 1 & 2 chose not to file the WS.
Hence, as such, it is deemed that they have admitted that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the respondent no.1.
Even otherwise, the respondent no.1 has been chargesheeted by the IO in the criminal case and the petitioner was unknown to respondent no.1 prior to the accident RUCHIKA by RUCHIKA SINGLA SINGLA

Date: 2025.12.20 15:11:43 +0530 and admittedly, there was no prior enmity with respondent no. 1 and hence, it is beyond comprehension as to why the petitioner will implicate respondent no.1 falsely, had he not been driving the offending vehicle.

18. It is pertinent to mention here that in the proceedings before the claims tribunal, the facts are to be established on the basis of preponderance of probabilities and not by the strict rules of evidence or the higher standard of beyond reasonable doubt as required in criminal cases.
The burden of proof in the present cases is much lower than as placed in civil or criminal cases.

In Bimla Devi &
Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SC 530, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that negligence must be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view must be adopted in reaching a conclusion.

"......where the claimants filed either the certified copies of the criminal record or the criminal record showing the completion of investigation by police or issuance of charge sheet under Section 279/304A IPC or the certified copy of FIR or the recovery of the mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle, then these documents are sufficient RUCHIKA by RUCHIKA SINGLA SINGLA Date: 2025.12.20 15:11:52 +0530 proof to reach to a conclusion that the driver was negligent particularly when there is no defence available from the side of driver."

sentences.text: 21. It is a settled law that the petitioner cannot be expected to prove the accident beyond reasonable doubts and the principle of res ipsa loquitor should apply which means that the "accident speaks for itself".

Thus, once it has been established in DAR and chargesheet that the accident had taken place,
the burden shifts on the respondents to prove that they were not responsible for the accident which the respondents have failed to discharge.
Hence, an adverse inference is drawn against the respondents.

In this regard, reliance is placed on the judgments of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the cases of Teja Singh Vs Suman & Ors., MAC. APP. 1111/2018 & CM APPL. 52384/2018,

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. (2018) 5 SCC 656 has laid down in paragraphs 27 & 28:
"27.

sentences.text: ...This Court in a recent decision in Dulcina Fernandes, noted that the key of negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle as set up by the claimants was required to be decided by the Tribunal on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and certainly not by standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt.

Suffice it to observe that the exposition in the judgments already adverted to by us, filing of chargesheet against Respondent 2 prima facie points towards his complicity in driving the vehicle negligently and rashly.

Further, even when the accused were to be acquitted in the criminal case, this Court opined that the same may be of no effect on the assessment of the liability required in respect of motor accident cases by the Tribunal.
28. Reliance placed upon the decisions in Minu B. Mehta and Meena Variyal, by the respondents, in our opinion, is of no avail.
The dictum in these cases is on the matter in issue in the case concerned.
Similarly, even the dictum in Surender Kumar Arora will be of no avail.

In the present case, considering the entirety of the pleadings,
evidence and circumstances on record and in particular the finding recorded by the Tribunal on the factum of negligence of Respondent 2, the driver of the offending jeep, the High Court committed manifest error in taking a contrary view which, in our opinion, is an error apparent on the face of record and manifestly wrong."

sentences.text: The Court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

(See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D. Hattangadi Vs.
Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467).
5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following :

sentences.text: Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured,
comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage).
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii)(a) and (iv)."
27.

In view of the above law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in injury cases, award needs to be passed only under heads of medical expenses, loss of earning during treatment period and damages for pain, suffering and trauma.

This is a case where the petitioner has claimed that he suffered grievous injury due to the accident, hence, this Tribunal now proceeds further step by step to decide the compensation/award under different heads applicable to the present matter in light of above preposition.
